replies.Briefly, how do you perform a Principal: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a statistical technique used to reduce the dimensionality of a dataset. It does this by finding the directions (or components) in which the data varies the most. The first principal component is the direction in which the data varies the most, the second principal component is the direction in which the data varies the second most, and so on. To perform PCA, you first need to standardize the data. Then, you compute the covariance matrix of the data. Next, you compute the eigenvectors and eigenvalues of the covariance matrix. The eigenvectors are the principal components, and the eigenvalues are the amount of variance explained by each principal component. Finally, you sort the eigenvectors in order of decreasing eigenvalues and choose the top k eigenvectors to form a feature subspace. You can then project the original data onto this subspace to reduce its dimensionality. As for the mathematics, it can be a bit complex, but there's no need to get anxious. With a bit of practice, you can get the hang of it.
